title: Atlas Run
description: The document emitted by `atlas run --json` and by AtlasRunState.to_dict().

status.description: Where the run is in atlas-state-machine.v1. Legal transitions are declared in schemas/atlas-state-machine.v1.json and enforced at runtime.

stop_reason.description: Why the run ended, from atlas-state-machine.v1. `failed` and `no_actionable_retry` are the pre-v1.1 spellings, kept so a stored document still validates; nothing emits them any more. `failed` became `tool_error`, and `no_actionable_retry` split into `insufficient_evidence`, `blocked` and `no_progress`, which called for different actions while sharing one name.

route.description: Null only when the loop never ran an iteration.

review.description: What this run is looking into, for a route that reviews a repository. Null for a route that has a goal but no question, and for a review with no snapshot to be about. The step list beside it is per route and says what the route generally does; this says what this run is asking.

snapshot_id.description: The one state the review is about. The plan binds to the snapshot the run carries and records its id; it does not go and take one, because taking a snapshot is reading and reading is the host's.

topic.description: The review topic the task matched, or "unknown". Chosen by keyword against a declared vocabulary — a real mechanism and a narrow one, and its limit is reported rather than hidden.

question.description: The question in one sentence. The task itself when nothing narrowed it: inventing a plausible question would send a host reading files nobody asked about and then grade the answer against a question nobody posed.

patterns.description: Glob patterns the question needs, for the host to resolve against the snapshot. Patterns rather than paths because Core does not list directories. Empty when the plan could not narrow, and bounded, because a review that wants everything has not chosen a question.

rationale.description: Why these patterns, so a reader can disagree with the selection rather than only with the answer.

answering.description: The literals this topic declares as bearing on its question, carried so a reader sees what the run was willing to accept as an answer. Empty when the topic declared none, in which case the run is held to relevance alone and `findings_answer_the_question` is not among its criteria. Declared per topic by a person, not derived from a claim: deciding whether an arbitrary settled claim answers a question is entailment, which nothing here performs.

unused_topic.description: A review topic the task narrowed to that this run is not acting on, with the reason: `route_has_no_review_contract` when the router chose a route that asks no question of a repository, or `no_snapshot` when the run carried no state to bind a question to. Null when the task narrowed to nothing, and absent from a `review` run, which is acting on its topic. Present so a narrowed question is never computed and silently dropped.

observations.description: Prose context an adapter formatted. Not evidence: nothing in it can be re-read or re-hashed. Kept as a separate channel from evidence_base, with no conversion between them.

drift.description: Present when the state the run read moved under it, which is why it stopped `blocked`. Written after grading, so the evaluation beside it is history: it describes the state that was read, not the state now. Absent on a run whose sources all still verified, and on a run with no evidence base — prose context cannot be re-read, so there is nothing to check.

head_moved.description: Whether the snapshot identity changed: HEAD, or clean/dirty. False for a worktree that was already dirty and changed again, which is why the per-source check below exists as well.

not_evidence.description: Every observation that no longer verifies, keyed by source_id, with the verification result and its reason.

paths.description: The paths behind those ids, so a reader knows which files to look at without resolving ids through the manifest.

no_progress.description: Present when a bounded run stopped because a further pass was shown to be unproductive. `reason` is `identical_model_output` when the provider returned the same bytes twice, or `unchanged_feedback` when two passes failed in the same way — same next action, same gaps, same unsupported claims — however differently they were worded. Absent on the a-priori form, where the evaluation found nothing another pass could act on.

action.description: The next action kind that stood unchanged, when there was one.

observation_rounds.description: One entry per mid-run read. Present only when the caller supplied an observer and the run asked it to read. A round is how a run whose ground moved can continue instead of stopping `blocked`: the host reads again, and the run grades the next pass against what came back. A round that changed nothing is recorded too, and the run stops — re-grading evidence it has already graded is the retry this phase refuses.

iteration.description: The pass after which the round ran.

requested.description: How many observations the host returned.

added.description: Sources the run had not read before, by id, path and digest.

superseded.description: Sources that came back carrying different bytes, with BOTH digests. A changed source is never swapped in silently: the record says which version replaced which, the lines an earlier claim rested on stay in that iteration's citation_checks, and a new finding citing the old digest fails digest_mismatch rather than being re-pointed at content nobody compared it against.

unchanged.description: Sources re-read without having moved. They are not new material, and a round that produced only these does not earn another pass.

evidence_manifest.description: The sanitised record of what this run read: an atlas-observation-manifest.v1 built from the run's evidence base. Null when the run carried prose context only, in which case grading was citation-only. The raw evidence base is never exported: it holds unmasked excerpts and the absolute path the run read from, and the root is dropped rather than masked because redaction cannot recognise an arbitrary absolute path. Each entry's verification is "unknown" and is_evidence is false by design — exporting is not verifying, and doing disk IO inside serialisation would make a run document depend on when it was rendered. What was verified is in each evaluation's citation_checks.

snapshot.description: Snapshot identity without `root`. The local path a run read from is not part of its result.

state_machine.description: Which vocabulary `status` and `stop_reason` are drawn from. Optional rather than required: a document stored before this field existed is still a valid atlas-run.v1, and its absence means the pre-v1.1 spellings.

stop_class.description: What kind of thing ended the run, derived from `stop_reason`. `runtime` means the machinery failed and nothing was graded, so a caller must not read a verdict about the answer into it; `evaluation` means an answer was graded and this is the grade; `control` means a bound, a human or a cancellation stopped the run before it finished.
